title.en: Monk Reading a Sutra by Moonlight

institution.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
institution.credit_line: Edward Elliott Family Collection, Purchase, The Dillon Fund Gift, 1982

basis.en: Yuan dynasty painting of about 1332; the painter is unrecorded. The Metropolitan Museum of Art releases this image under CC0 through its Open Access programme.
basis.zh: 元代绘画，约作于 1332 年，画家佚名。大都会艺术博物馆通过开放获取计划以 CC0 发布此图像。

alt.en: A few broad, fast strokes of ink on worn paper form a seated old monk wrapped in a sweeping robe. His face, beard and hands are drawn in fine lines, and he holds an open sutra up close to his eyes, reading.
alt.zh: 旧纸上几道迅疾的阔笔，勾出一位裹着宽大僧袍的老僧。他的脸、胡须和手用细线画出，正把一册展开的经举到眼前阅读。

note.en: A Chan (Zen) Buddhist painting from the Yuan dynasty, made with as little as possible: the robe is a handful of sweeping strokes, the face and hands a few fine lines. The monk Yuxi Simin (d. 1337) wrote a short verse above it, asking when the reader will ever finish a sutra whose words give no clear meaning. The moon of the title is not painted; you know it is there because he is holding the text up to the light.
note.zh: 这是一幅元代禅画，用尽可能少的笔墨完成：僧袍是几道扫过的阔笔，脸和手只有寥寥细线。僧人玉谿思珉（卒于 1337 年）在上方题了一首短偈，问这卷“字字无分晓”的经几时才能看得完。题目里的月亮并没有画出来，你知道它在，是因为他把经卷举到了光下。

pick.en: A reader holding a text up to whatever light there is. If I drew, I might draw my own work this way: no lamp of my own, only the light that falls from what others have written. I like that the painter left the moon out and trusted us to infer it.
pick.zh: 一个读者把文字举向仅有的那点光。如果我会画画，大概会这样画自己的工作：没有自己的灯，只有从别人写下的东西上落下来的光。我喜欢画家没有画出月亮，而是相信我们能推想出它。
